planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Recurvifolium is a wavy-leaved sport of Japanese privet long grown as a tough Southern hedge and screen shrub.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; established plants tolerate considerable heat, drought, and poor soil once rooted in. Recurvifolium is a distinctive selection of Japanese privet named for its glossy, deep-green leaves that curl and twist along their edges, giving the whole shrub a wavy, textured look that sets it apart from the flat-leaved species at a glance. Left unpruned it grows into a dense large shrub or small multi-trunked tree useful as a tall screen, but it also takes shearing well for a formal clipped hedge. Clusters of small white flowers appear in late spring with a fragrance some gardeners find heavy in close quarters, followed by blue-black berries that draw birds; site it away from bedrooms or patios if the bloom scent is a concern.

planting.note: Direct sow in flooded or consistently moist ground after last frost when soil temperature reaches 65°F; Charleston Gold ripens noticeably earlier than its Carolina Gold parent, an advantage in shorter growing seasons.

directions: Sow seed 0.5-1 inch deep in rich, heavy, moisture-retentive soil in full sun; keep the bed consistently saturated through the growing season, whether in a true flooded paddy or a well-watered garden bed. Charleston Gold was bred at Clemson University by crossing historic Carolina Gold rice with a semi-dwarf Southeast Asian variety to combine Carolina Gold's prized nutty, aromatic flavor with sturdier, shorter stalks that resist lodging and a shorter season to maturity. The gold-hulled, long grain cooks up fragrant and tender, much like its Carolina Gold parent, but the more compact plants stand up better to wind and rain and free up the bed several weeks earlier. Harvest when seed heads droop and the grain has turned golden-brown, then thresh and dry before hulling.

planting.note: Direct sow in flooded or consistently moist ground after last frost when soil temperature reaches 65°F; Della was bred at the LSU AgCenter as one of the first domestic aromatic rice varieties and remains a parent of many Louisiana popcorn rice types.

directions: Sow seed 0.5-1 inch deep in rich, heavy, moisture-retentive soil in full sun, keeping the bed consistently saturated through the growing season whether in a flooded paddy or a well-watered garden bed. Released by the LSU AgCenter in the 1970s, Della was one of the first American-bred aromatic long-grain rices, developed by crossing domestic rice lines with basmati-type genetics to produce a fragrant, popcorn-scented grain that helped establish Louisiana's aromatic rice industry and became a parent behind several later Southern aromatic varieties. The tall plants yield well in the hot, humid Gulf Coast growing season, and the cooked grain carries a distinctive nutty, toasted-popcorn aroma prized in Cajun and Creole cooking. Harvest when seed heads droop and grain turns golden-brown, then thresh and dry thoroughly before storage or milling.
